key_insight: RayPE replaces purely image-grid-based positional encoding with ray-space geometry, so a video model can reason about where camera rays intersect or relate in 3D space. The key idea is that the Plücker reciprocal product between rays matches the bilinear structure already used in Transformer attention.
problem_solved: Standard video diffusion transformers use positional encodings over (u, v, t), which describe pixel and time coordinates but ignore the 3D geometry of the scene. This makes it harder for models to generate videos that stay consistent with camera motion and scene structure.
method: Extend positional encoding into ray space by encoding camera rays rather than only 2D pixel-time coordinates.
Use the Plücker reciprocal product to capture geometric relations between pairs of rays in a form compatible with attention.
Inject ray-aware positional information into the transformer so token interactions reflect 3D scene geometry.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, RayPE offers a principled way to improve 3D-aware video generation without redesigning the entire transformer architecture. It can help models produce more geometrically consistent and camera-aware videos, especially for scenes with viewpoint changes.

paper_title: RayPE: Ray-Space Positional Encoding for 3D-Aware Video Generation
paper_authors: Minghao Yin, Jiahao Lu, Wenbo Hu, Wang Zhao, Shan Ying
